content.overview: Article 242 dealt with the administration of Coorg as a distinct unit. It was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1 November 1956) when Coorg was merged into the State of Mysore (now Karnataka) under States reorganisation.
content.glance: Art 242 omitted by 7th Amendment 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Coorg merged into Mysore (Karnataka).
content.study:
Article 242 provided for Coorg as a separate administrative unit under Part VIII arrangements.

Omission: Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956), implementing States reorganisation; Coorg was integrated into Mysore.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 242 as living law. Coorg (Kodagu) is part of Karnataka.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Omitted by the 7th Amendment, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Coorg ceased to be a separate constitutional unit and became part of Mysore (Karnataka).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 242?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 242 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956) when Coorg was merged into Mysore. It is not living law.
